title: A batch runner's standing duty is a rolling combine train, written into decision session-tiers and the project-ops batch-runner template
why: Owner 21:48 CST Nov 13, in runner 10's chat (relayed by the consultant): the combining should be continuous, with lane PRs always joining a batch, so the runner becomes a scaling machine; if sound, make it part of how a batch runner is briefed and operates. Owner item 826 01:57 CST Nov 14 (pick-pause-combine-tournament, consultant 01:55, relayed): the consultant reports 9 combine PRs opened since 21:45 CST Nov 13, 0 merged (4 closed, 5 open), all 7 claude-settings merges single PRs; Degen merged 10 single PRs per lane 00:36-01:43. Triage REST read (partial, 30 most recently closed to 04:06 UTC): 6 combine PRs closed unmerged (#3360, #3361, #3363, #3314, #3315, #3356), none merged; 6 single PRs merged. Question to the owner: pause (a, consultant recommends: merge alone by priority, combine only to clear a real conflict, review after 10 merges) or keep (b). Nothing changes until he answers. Item 826 reframed 02:17 CST Nov 14 (consultant 02:14, relayed): main already merges per lane (decision all-repos-switch-together, owner 09:42 CST Nov 12; R42); the one open question is whether to keep ruling own-rolling-combine-train (21:48 CST Nov 13). Options now: a withdraw the train and stay per-lane plus quick dry checks before each ready mark (consultant recommends); b keep it, built as designed and automated, review after 3 batches. Nothing changes until the owner answers.
source: Consultant 21:49 CST Nov 13, relaying runner 10 relaying the owner; retrospective agrees.
note: Triage 21:49 CST Nov 13: duty as the consultant states it: a batch closes when its real PR is built and linted, later hand-ins join the next batch, clashing members leave by name. Each merge report carries per-batch numbers: members in, members left out, clash rate, dry-round minutes, lint minutes and CI minutes. Review after 3 batches against lone merges: does the train save time. Homes: decision session-tiers (batch runner) and the project-ops batch-runner template, via a lane the coordinator assigns; a fresh reviewer reads it, since it changes a role's duty. Rule: no rule or guard changes here; merges stay serial. Unmeasured by triage: whether a train beats lone merges; the review is how that gets measured. Coordinator 21:50 CST Nov 13 (21:50): lane started, session_013NEJL2vjqFYDAqvgfkZRN3 (Sonnet, medium). Scope: the duty in two homes, decision session-tiers (batch runner section) and the project-ops batch-runner template; the template points to the decision, no copy; no rule or guard change; a fresh reviewer reads it. Overlap by title search (unchecked by triage), open PRs touching those files: #3259, #3247, #3159, #3117, #3057, #2920, #2860, #2747, #2709, #2701. The lane reads each diff, makes its edit a small additive section, and names "Merge after: ...". Path: a combined docs PR via runner 10, in the next batch. Owner 21:52 CST (relayed by the consultant; ruling own-rolling-combine-train part 2): the batch in CI and the next in line are frozen; every batch behind them keeps folding into one, even after their lints ran, until CI finishes on main. The lane's homes must say so. After a fold the combined head is linted again, since it is a new head (triage reading; unchecked). Owner 21:54 CST (ruling own-rolling-combine-train part 3): levels L1 sort, L2 combine lane PRs, L3 fold batches behind the next in line, L4 the frozen next-in-line and in-CI batch; all by the batch runner's agents; runner 10 drafts the level table into the wave plan. The lane's homes name the levels. Lane report 23:17 CST Nov 13 (lane session_013NEJL2vjqFYDAqvgfkZRN3, unchecked by triage): #3341 (head 53893febf3, done) and follow-up #3357 (head 2bca8bdc6f, done, merge after #3341) are with runner 10, lane lint PASS on both. The lane says the note's "frozen pair" and "pin the next-in-line head" are the consultant's readings, written as open in the decision, not rulings. Owner ruling 01:55 CST Nov 14 (own-ready-by-priority, relayed by the consultant): marking a PR ready is not instant; the runner thinks about priority because a ready PR can hog CI from lanes that need it first. The consultant's reading, unconfirmed as the owner's intent: ready in priority order, only while CI has free slots (macOS scarce), one priority order shared by the three runners. The lane writes the duty into session-tiers and the template only as far as the owner's words go, and names the rest as a pick. Second owner word 01:54 CST Nov 14 (own-ready-by-priority, via the consultant 01:54): "the number of slots cant be a static number btw it can change yk": the runner reads live queue state (queued jobs per leg) before each ready mark; no fixed slot number. Coordinator's reading (relayed): wave-plan priority order, CI-speed first; slots measured from queued-job times; one order across the three runners.
